purpose: Three coupled trainer.py fixes for book-spine bf16 fine-tuning. (1) Gradient accumulation loss scaling: scale ONLY the backward loss by 1/accum_steps when gradient_accumulation_steps > 1, so accumulating N micro-batch gradients equals the gradient of the MEAN loss over those micro-batches (true effective-batch semantics at unchanged learning rate); logged losses and the finite-check keep the raw unscaled value; optimizer/scheduler/clipping timing is unchanged; accum=1 is bit-for-bit identical. (2) bf16 AMP loss-scaling safety: GradScaler is enabled ONLY when amp_dtype==float16 (it is unnecessary and unsafe under bfloat16 -- the scale backs off toward 0 and once 1/scale overflows fp32 the unscale step turns finite grads into NaN/Inf while found_inf stays 0, corrupting every weight; empirically reproduced on torch 2.10.0+cu128). (3) [GRAD-GUARD] non-finite gradient guard + stop policy: detect non-finite grads BEFORE clipping (reusing the total norm the clip needs -- one fused pass; the per-parameter first-non-finite-param scan runs only on the rare bad step and is logged as a LOCATING HINT, not a proven root-cause layer), skip the optimizer step (zero_grad) when grads are inf/nan, and FAIL CLOSED via FloatingPointError on GRAD_GUARD_MAX_CONSECUTIVE_SKIPS=3 consecutive skips or a >10% skip ratio over the last 200 optimizer steps, so training cannot silently 'finish' without updating the model. Skip counters (total/consecutive/rolling window) are persisted in the checkpoint, restored on resume, and logged to tensorboard + trainer state. Root cause addressed: run 2026-07-23_13-25-53 epoch-7 all-1093-weights-NaN crash.
